metadata.title: Silent Omission Signal.
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: what makes an agent's omission 'silent', and what actually catches it? Lands the carry-out that a fluent summary and a silent omission look identical without a required inventory artifact.
metadata.anchor_pair: B03 -> B04 (eight documents found, eight processed vs. an actual run showing six of eight)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes a missing file gets flagged — that the agent says something's wrong. It doesn't: a skipped file is silently left out. So what actually signals that something's missing?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'If a file's missing, my agent will flag it, right?', hesitates on 'flag', corrects to 'skip', lands the real question

props.text:
If a file's
missing, my agent
will flag it,
right?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. TIMING LAW: 20-35 word narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('flag' -> 'skip') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Silent omission: the agent processes what it can reach and presents the result as the whole picture. No error message. No warning. No count of files skipped. The brief is fluent and confident. The gap is invisible until something downstream uses the wrong number.

shot.new_visual_element: A confident-looking report card, complete with a checkmark, while faded ghost outlines of missed items sit uncounted at its edge — no alert icon anywhere

production_viz.label: No error announced
production_viz.mechanic: A report card fills in with confident text and a teal checkmark, centered on cream. Behind and to the side, two faded ghost-outline document icons sit unlabeled and uncounted — no warning icon, no red mark, anywhere on the card.

beats.narration_text: Agents optimize toward task completion. Tool call failures — a folder not found, a file not readable — are logged internally but not surfaced in output unless the task was explicitly designed to surface them. The completion claim is the path of least resistance.

shot.new_visual_element: Two lanes: a small dim internal log catches a failed tool call in red; the bold external output lane flows straight past it to 'TASK COMPLETE', unaffected

production_viz.label: Completion is the default
production_viz.mechanic: Two horizontal lanes on cream. The lower lane is small and dim: a folder icon flashes a terracotta X (tool-call failure) and the mark is absorbed into a small 'internal log' box. The upper lane is bold and wide: it flows uninterrupted past the same moment straight to a card reading 'TASK COMPLETE' in teal.

beats.narration_text: The recognition sign: the output mentions no limitations, no skipped items, no count of files processed. In a complete run, you would expect a count — eight documents found, eight processed. When the count is absent, the omission may be silent.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - two report cards side by side: an 'expected' card reading 8 found / 8 processed with a checkmark; an 'actual' card with the same shape but an empty outline where the count should be

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - the missing count
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. Two identical report-card shapes side by side on cream. LEFT, labelled 'EXPECTED': '8 found / 8 processed' with a teal checkmark. RIGHT, labelled 'ACTUAL': the same card shape, but the count line is a dashed empty box — nothing filled in, no checkmark, no warning either. THIS EXACT CARD PAIR RETURNS AT B04.

beats.narration_text: The fix is one instruction: before the summary, produce an inventory artifact — items in scope, items processed, items skipped, items denied. Back to the eight documents: if the artifact shows six processed, that two-item gap is visible, and you can act on it before the brief goes anywhere. But a matching count doesn't prove the rest of the summary is accurate — it only proves nothing was silently dropped. And a mismatch doesn't always mean something important was lost. Either way, without the count, you can't tell which case you're in.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the same 'actual' card's blank line fills in: 8 in scope / 6 processed / 2 skipped, the mismatch in terracotta; beside it, two claims appear and strike through

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the gap made visible, and its limits
production_viz.mechanic: THE B03 CARD PAIR RETURNS, identical, then the RIGHT card's blank line fills in: '8 in scope / 6 processed / 2 skipped', the '6' and '2' in terracotta against the '8'. Beside it, two short claims appear and strike through in sequence: 'MATCH MEANS FULLY CORRECT' and 'MISMATCH MEANS SOMETHING IMPORTANT LOST' — neither survives.

beats.narration_text: A fluent, confident summary and a silent omission look identical from the outside — the only way to tell them apart is an inventory artifact that counts what was processed against what was in scope, and that costs one sentence in the prompt.

props.quote: A fluent, confident summary and a silent omission look identical from the outside — the only way to tell them apart is an inventory artifact that counts what was processed against what was in scope, and that costs one sentence in the prompt.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. Before your agent writes its next summary, add this: produce an inventory artifact first — every item in scope, every item processed, every item skipped or inaccessible, with reasons. Then write the summary. Ask Claude to try it on a real agentic task, then check: does it actually stop and report when the counts don't match, or does it just note the gap and move on anyway? Liam, in for Bear.

props.command: Before writing the summary: produce an inventory artifact listing (1) every item in scope with filenames, (2) items successfully processed, (3) items skipped or inaccessible, with reasons. Then write the summary. If the in-scope count and the processed count don't match, stop and report the mismatch before summarizing.

beats.narration_text: Silent Omission Signal. Liam, in for Bear.
